chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying, and he was asked about a man who bought a slave girl, then had intercourse with her before she had completed her istibra' (period of waiting to confirm pregnancy). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done. He should seek forgiveness from Allah and not repeat (the act of selling without istibra' or the specific fault).'

I said, 'Suppose he sold her to another, and did not clear her womb (did not perform istibra'), then the second owner sold her to another man, so he had intercourse with her, and did not clear her womb, so her pregnancy became manifest in the presence of the third?'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (the last owner who had intercourse with her), and for the adulterer (or the one who had intercourse without full certainty of lineage) are the stones.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الِاسْتِبْرَاءُ: The period of waiting for a female slave or divorcee to confirm she is not pregnant before she can be married or sold.
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: The child belongs to the bed (the last husband/owner who had intercourse with her), a key principle of lineage.
key_terms.لِلْعَاهِرِ الْحَجَرُ: For the adulterer (or one with uncertain lineage) are the stones (a reference to a hadith about stoning or bearing the burden of uncertainty).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child's lineage if a slave girl is sold multiple times without proper istibra'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'al-waladu lil-firash' (the child belongs to the one whose bed it is) in the context of slave ownership, emphasizing that the last owner to have sexual relations with the slave girl before birth holds the right to the offspring. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the legal presumption of paternity for the owner and the potential liability for the 'adulterer' (or subsequent owner) if lineage is disputed, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding property and lineage. The ruling underscores the importance of 'istibra'' (clearing the womb) to prevent uncertainty in inheritance and family structure.
